_comment: Macro-scale reproduction for #1616. A 30-wide single-rank AI-controlled Cavalry regiment (team 1, frontage_override 30, so Unit.terrain_clearance() is huge, ~590wu) spawns near the default map's hill patch (Battle.TERRAIN rect (1150,380)-(1400,580), kind 'block') facing AWAY from a stationary team-0 Infantry target -- the initial bearing from facing [0,1] to the target direction is ~112 degrees, past Unit.FACING_SNAP_ABSORB_THRESHOLD (75 degrees), so once UnitLeader.decide's own nearest-enemy fallback issues an explicit ATTACK order on the very first _run_enemy_ai() call (tick 0 -- Battle._apply_order_cmd sets target_enemy and current_order = ATTACK from it), Unit._think's explicit-target chase branch (target_enemy != null, not the separate auto-advance-on-detect fallback further down, which never sets current_order and so could not produce this scenario's own current_order == ATTACK expectation) drives Unit._move_to's formed_turn branch into the SNAP path -- facing is set directly from the funnel-corner waypoint via _face_dir every decision, not throttled through a gradual pivot the way a player order's pivot_as_formation branch is. PathField._segment_blocked's room-capped clearance-grown margin around the hill still spuriously blocks the direct leg to the target (same mechanism as the earlier close-tier repro), and pre-fix, _funnel_corner's corner selection flip-flops nearly every tick -- the SNAPPED facing follows whichever ~170-degree-apart waypoint is current that tick, a macro-scale whipsaw the automated facing_whipsaw defect check can actually detect (unlike a throttled player-move demo, whose swings this same bug caps below the detector's 10-degree floor). Both units stay well under FormationTier.PROMOTE_RANGE (400wu) and never make contact within this clip's window, so this is genuinely close-tier and isolated to the pivot itself -- no scripted player steps needed; team 1's own AI drives the whole chase. `state` is per-tick from the AI's order dispatch (already ATTACK by tick 8) through tick 120 -- the clip's own last covered physics tick, since demo.1616.json's max_frames 60 at fixed_fps 30 covers max_frames * 60 / fixed_fps = 120 physics ticks, so the verified window now matches the full recorded clip: pre-fix this flip-flops on nearly every one of those ticks (66 sign reversals at facing_whipsaw's own 10-degree swing floor); post-fix it takes exactly one legitimate snap (tick 81->82, once the slowly-diverging bearing finally crosses the 75-degree absorb threshold) and holds that heading cleanly through the rest of the window.
